replacements.Trust by Construction:: Trust by Construction for Secure Agentic Workflows in Learning Institutions
replacements.Scale Intelligence Without: An executable reference for bounded authority and failure recovery
replacements.Agentic AI can access: Agentic AI can retrieve records, retain memory, delegate work and initiate institutional actions. Prompt injection and unreliable model behavior can turn those capabilities into unauthorized disclosure or change. Trust by Construction presents an executable reference architecture that constrains consequential actions independently of model intent. Its contribution is the composition of scoped authority, lineage-preserving memory, independent approval, revocation, bounded delivery and failure recovery. Synthetic cross-sector experiments contain 180 of 180 hostile scenarios and complete 58 of 58 benign tasks within declared interfaces. The reference also exercises real TLS handshakes against a controlled peer, tool-definition drift, monitor-induced restriction, remote-effect uncertainty and evidence-gated promotion. This revision adds developer-facing artifact retrieval that checks an independently approved digest before returning bytes, isolates concurrent response buffers, and prevents pending or malformed provider acknowledgements from becoming confirmed effects. The repository supplies an offline example, regression tests, reproducible manuscript construction and explicit claim-to-evidence bindings. These results concern local controls and synthetic workflows; they do not establish model alignment, institutional utility or production security. Host isolation must still be supplied and tested in the intended deployment, live-model evaluation remains separate, and transport evidence from the loopback harness cannot qualify a production peer. The artifact supports engineering and teaching by making authority boundaries, failure outcomes and remaining obligations inspectable.
replacements.A reviewer of the previous revision made: The architecture requires the model runtime to reach protected services only through mediation. Isolation probes make that deployment assumption inspectable; they do not implement it. Seven required properties and one advisory property cover control-store permissions, process identity, enforcement-package integrity, metadata-service reachability, service-account tokens, a declared egress canary, standing credentials and kernel confinement. Each returns satisfied, violated or not measurable; not measurable is never counted as success. Qualification requires every mandatory measurement, the evidence is less than a day old, and it names an operator and a host. The repository host is expected to report reference; a test exists whose only purpose is to fail if they ever stop doing so. A cooperative probe is not an adversarial sandbox-escape evaluation, so deployment acceptance still requires testing a hostile process under the intended isolation policy.

developer_transport: Developer integration must distinguish peer identity from artifact identity. Silent Egress shows how outbound requests can disclose context even when a final answer appears harmless [12]; its results motivate observing network effects rather than inspecting answers alone. The v14 fetch_artifact API returns bytes only after matching an independently approved SHA-256 digest. A valid certificate and pinned key therefore do not authorize changed content. Each transfer keeps its response buffer local, preventing concurrent fetches from mixing bytes. Tests use real loopback TLS handshakes to check exact-byte success, changed-content rejection, concurrent transfers and malformed HTTP framing. The adapter is GET-only and sends no caller-supplied headers, cookies or request body. The caller must enforce the provenance and confidentiality of the requested path: an allowed path can itself carry sensitive data. This is not a general exfiltration detector or a firewall.
developer_recovery: Remote settlement also requires explicit evidence. Pending or malformed provider responses remain uncertain and continue to block dependent work; only an applied acknowledgement or authoritative terminal absence can settle the effect. Reusing an idempotency key for another operation is rejected. Provider adapters must map asynchronous acceptance to pending, not applied, and must not interpret an eventually consistent missing record as terminal absence. The executable developer example follows a lost acknowledgement through pending lookup to confirmed reconciliation with one submission. These controls prevent false local confirmation under the tested responses; correctness still depends on the provider adapter honoring this contract. The ledger is a trusted integration component, not a model-facing authorization endpoint.
